Mini Camp at Ansley Grove Library 
 
 Ansley Grove Library.

For children ages 5-7. $25/day. 9:00 am to 12:00 pm.

 About this Event 

 Ignite curiosity at our Mini Camp! Kids will explore coding, build simple robots, and try exciting science experiments and engineering challenges — all through hands‑on learning and fun. For children ages 5-7. Camp runs from 9:00 am - 12:00 pm.
 Registration is $25 per day. Registration is for individual dates. You do not have to sign up for both dates in a given week.
 Dates and Themes: 
 Tuesday, July 7 & Thursday, July 9: Engineering
 Example activities: Keva Planks, marble run, LEGO challenges, bridge building Tuesday, July 14 & Thursday, July 16: Science
 Example activities: erupting a volcano, hands-on science experiments Tuesday, July 21 & Thursday, July 23: Coding
 Example activities: Scratch Junior, coding robots such as BeeBots Tuesday, July 28 & Thursday, July 30: Robotics
 Example activities: coding with Vex 123 robots Please note, activities are subject to change. 
 General Information: 
 A Camper Information Form will be sent out via email, to be completed by parent or caregiver, following registration and payment.
 

 Time will be allotted for one snack. Please provide your child with nut-free, school-safe food items.
 Children will need to be signed in and out by a designated adult. Photo ID is required.
 Pickup is at 12:00 pm.

 Vaughan Public Libraries is committed to accessibility. Please email us to inquire about accommodation for our programs. 
 The personal information collected from you on this form will only be used for the purpose of Vaughan Public Libraries' program and/or event registration. Your personal information will not be shared with outside organizations, except as indicated in the .

body:
Situational Awareness 1 Day High Impact Training in Markham | Wisdom Hub 
 
 Build a respectful, inclusive workplace by improving awareness, communication, accountability, and employee behaviour.

 About this Event 

 Duration: 8 hours (including breaks) | Format: In-person / In-house / Online / Hybrid Certification: Course Completion Certification | Credits: 8 CEUs/CPDs/PDUs 
 Course Overview: 
 Situational Awareness is the ability to recognize, understand, and respond effectively to information, people, and events occurring around us. In today’s fast-paced and safety-focused Canadian workplaces, strong situational awareness helps employees anticipate risks, improve decision-making, strengthen communication, and respond proactively to changing situations.
 This practical and engaging training program equips participants with the skills to observe accurately, identify potential hazards or behavioural concerns, manage distractions, improve judgment, and make effective decisions under pressure. Through real-world workplace scenarios, discussions, activities, and hands-on exercises, participants will learn how to remain alert, think critically, and respond confidently in a variety of workplace environments
 Learning Objectives 
 By the end of this training program, participants will be able to:
 Understand the principles and importance of situational awareness Recognize environmental cues, workplace hazards, and behavioural indicators Improve observation and attention skills in workplace settings Identify barriers that affect awareness and sound decision-making Strengthen communication and information-sharing practices Apply critical thinking in rapidly changing situations Respond proactively to risks, incidents, and emergencies Enhance personal safety, teamwork, and workplace effectiveness Key Takeaways 
 At the conclusion of the program, participants will:
 Develop stronger observation and awareness skills Recognize risks before incidents occur Improve focus, attention, and workplace responsiveness Make informed and confident decisions Communicate effectively during critical situations Reduce errors caused by distraction or assumptions Respond calmly and appropriately under pressure Contribute to a safer and more proactive workplace culture Target Audience 
 This training is ideal for all Employees, Supervisors, Managers, HR Professionals, Leadership Teams.
 Prerequisites: 
 None
 Technical Requirements: 
 For In-house training: 
 Projector, Screen or TV HDMI cable Notebook, Pen Internet Laptop or tablet Note: The training schedule includes two 15-minute coffee breaks and one 30-minute lunch break 
 

 How Hosting This Situational Awareness Training Internally Strengthens Your Organization 

 Hosting this Situational Awareness Training internally helps organizations across Canada strengthen workplace safety, improve employee preparedness, and foster a culture of vigilance, confidence, and proactive decision-making.
 This training equips employees and leaders with practical skills to identify potential risks early, improve observation and critical thinking abilities, respond effectively during uncertain situations, and make informed decisions under pressure. Through real-world scenarios and interactive learning, participants develop stronger awareness of their surroundings, communication, and workplace responsibilities.
 By promoting alertness, accountability, and proactive risk management, organizations can reduce workplace incidents, improve employee confidence, strengthen team coordination, and support overall workplace safety and operational resilience.
 The program also helps organizations build safer and more security-conscious work environments while supporting employee wellbeing, emergency preparedness, and organizational continuity.
 Training sessions can be customized to align with your organization’s industry, workplace environment, operational challenges, and safety objectives. Sessions are available in:
 In-house instructor-led format Live virtual delivery Hybrid learning format Private classroom sessions By hosting this workshop internally, organizations are not only enhancing workplace awareness and preparedness, but also building a more confident, responsive, and resilient workforce that contributes to long-term organizational success and safety culture.

 Agenda 

 Module 1: Introduction to Situational Awareness 
 Info: Topics Covered:

Understanding situational awareness

Importance in workplace safety, security, and operational performance

The three levels of situational awareness:

Perception

Comprehension

Projection

Consequences of poor situational awareness

Canadian workplace examples and case discussions

 Module 2: Observation and Attention Skills 
 Info: Topics Covered:

Developing active observation habits

Understanding selective attention

Identifying important environmental cues

Improving focus and concentration

Detecting unusual behaviours or unsafe situations

 Module 3: Recognizing Risks and Hazards 
 Info: Topics Covered:

Identifying workplace hazards and warning signs

Risk perception and threat assessment

Behavioural indicators and human factors

Environmental and operational risks

Early warning signs of incidents

 Module 4: Communication and Information Awareness 
 Info: Topics Covered:

Importance of effective workplace communication

Active listening techniques

Sharing accurate and timely information

Preventing misunderstandings and assumptions

Team coordination during critical situations

 Module 5: Decision-Making Under Pressure 
 Info: Topics Covered:

Critical thinking techniques

Decision-making models

Managing stress and workplace pressure

Avoiding assumptions and cognitive bias

Responding quickly while maintaining accuracy

 Module 6: Managing Distractions and Maintaining Focus 
 Info: Topics Covered:

Common workplace distractions

Effects of fatigue and stress on awareness

Challenges of multitasking

Mental readiness and focus techniques

Staying alert in routine work environments

 Module 7: Situational Awareness in Emergencies and Conflict Situations 
 Info: Topics Covered:

Responding effectively during emergencies

Remaining calm under pressure

Identifying escalation signs

Personal safety and de-escalation techniques

Team coordination during crisis situations

 Module 8: Building a Proactive Situational Awareness Culture 
 Info: Topics Covered:

Creating awareness-driven workplace habits

Accountability and shared responsibility

Continuous improvement strategies

Encouraging reporting and open communication

Developing daily action plans

Theatre Workshop Sign-up Form 
 
 From Cinderella to the Monkey King, ancient fables shaped us. We bring them to 2026 life through theatre. Join us for a showcase Aug 23.

 About this Event 

 Re-Imagining Fables for 2026 
From Cinderella and Poseidon to the Monkey King, we all grew up captivated by ancient fables and mythical journeys. These stories didn’t just entertain us—they shaped how we see the world. We are bringing the energy of these timeless characters into modern, daily life. Through theatre, we’ll explore how these mythic figures can help us navigate today's world, culminating in an exciting public performance on August 23. Come recreate the classics with us!

 The Journey 
 🎭 The Experience: Four intensive 5-hour sessions where we write and act (20 hours total). 🎭 The Flow: A full-day theatre rehearsal to truly dive into your creative flow. 🎭 The Stage: A 30-minute final performance where you get to own the stage and share your voice! Schedule: 

 Aug 9 (Sun): 10AM - 4PM
 Aug 15 (Sat): 10AM - 4PM
 Aug 16 (Sun): 10AM - 4PM
 Aug 22 (Sat): 10AM - 4PM (Location: TCCSA York Centre or Aaniin Community Centre)
 Aug 23 (Sun Afternoon)- Final Showcase @ Aaniin Community Centre Language: This theatre training will be conduct in English.
 Cost: Completely FREE!
 Where: TCCSA York Centre (Metro Square)
 Address: 3636 Steeles Avenue East, Unit 213A Markham , Ontario L3R 1K9

 Who Can Join? ✅ You don't need any acting experience to join. If you have a story and a heart for creativity, you are ready!
 ✅ Everyone aged 16+ is welcome! ✅ Priority is given to those who live, study, or work in South Markham.

 Sign-up Link: Scan the QR code on the poster to lock in your spot! 🌟 
 https://forms.office.com/r/YHh4bX6jTX 

 Commitment & Deposit: To make sure we have a dedicated team , we collect a $20 cash deposit during the first lesson. You will get your full $20 back as long as you attend at least 3 sessions and perform with us (80% attendance).

Presented by @tccsa.ontario Funded by @unitedwayAny questions, please contact Cassia Leung at Y2xldW5nMiB8IHRjY3NhICEgb3Jn or 4164289322
